summary: Comprehensive test of new Active Sessions admin panel + JWT revocation across web/mobile. Backend: 5/5 pytest tests passing (list shape/header, revoke web session invalidates token but keeps others, mobile jwt-auth session lifecycle with revoke → jwt-me & jwt-refresh 401, inactive user login rejected 403 & existing token rejected 403, logout revokes token). Frontend: full Sessions page flow verified — sidebar System > Sessions navigation, table renders with User/Device/IP/Started/Expires/Status/Action columns, Current badge + WEB type badge shown on admin's own row with 'This device' button DISABLED, Refresh/search/show-revoked toggle all functional, logout returns to login. No critical issues found.
critical_code_review_comments: routes_sessions.py imports from server (api_router, db, log_audit, _require_admin, JWT_SECRET, JWT_ALGORITHM) — solid, no circular import issues. Cleanly separates admin session mgmt.

POST /api/users always sets password to DEFAULT_USER_PASSWORD (bpr2026) regardless of payload — the UserCreate model still declares a password field, giving false expectation. Consider dropping the password field from UserCreate or honoring it. Not blocking for this feature but noted.
list_sessions currently returns raw list with pagination via X-Total-Count header; consider also exposing skip/limit in UI (currently hardcoded to limit=500) for very large deployments.
SessionsPage.jsx (310 lines) is under the 700-line threshold; clean structure with proper data-testids on all interactive elements.
seed_data_creation: Test creates & deletes throwaway TEST_ users and TEST_pytest mobile sessions. Admin mobile device binding is cleared before/after mobile test. All test artifacts (leftover TEST_ users, admin mobile binding) cleaned post-run via mongo.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The Sessions feature is complete and working end-to-end. test_sessions.py is the regression suite; env vars ADMIN_EMAIL/ADMIN_PASSWORD/REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL must be set (conftest autouse fixture requires them). Mobile-auth test clears admin's mobile_device binding via direct mongo to bypass the 'already linked' guard — this is intentional because there is no admin-facing unbind-self endpoint (unbind is per user_id via /api/users/{id}/unbind-device). Sessions collection uses TTL and self-cleans; leftover revoked/expired rows appear in Show-revoked view but are harmless.
